# Pixel sort

Sorts runs of pixels by brightness or hue along rows or columns, the glitch-art streaks of pixel sorting. Only pixels between two brightness thresholds move.

<EffectDemo effect="pixel-sort" />

## Usage

```ts
import { EffectComposer } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { pixelSort } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/pixel-sort';

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer);
composer.setScene(scene, camera);
composer.add(pixelSort({ preset: 'waterfall' }));
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => composer.render());
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.low = 0.1`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling.

## Parameters

| Parameter    | Type                       | Default        | Range    | Description                                                                       |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `low`        | number                     | `0.1`          | 0 – 1    | Pixels darker than this stay put and end sorted runs.                             |
| `high`       | number                     | `0.9`          | 0 – 1    | Pixels brighter than this stay put and end sorted runs.                           |
| `direction`  | 'horizontal' \| 'vertical' | `'vertical'`   |          | Sort along rows or columns.                                                       |
| `sortBy`     | 'brightness' \| 'hue'      | `'brightness'` |          | What pixels are sorted by.                                                        |
| `reverse`    | boolean                    | `false`        |          | Sort in descending order.                                                         |
| `iterations` | integer                    | `64`           | 4 – 256  | Sorting steps; each lets a pixel move one place, so more make longer streaks.     |
| `resolution` | number                     | `0.5`          | 0.25 – 1 | Sorting buffer size relative to the frame; lower is faster and stretches streaks. |
| `amount`     | number                     | `1`            | 0 – 1    | Mix between the original and the sorted image.                                    |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset       | Settings                                                     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `waterfall`  | `direction: 'vertical'`, `iterations: 160`, `low: 0.05`      |
| `rainbow`    | `sortBy: 'hue'`, `direction: 'horizontal'`, `iterations: 96` |
| `highlights` | `low: 0.3`, `high: 1`, `iterations: 128`                     |
| `shadows`    | `low: 0`, `high: 0.4`, `reverse: true`                       |

Apply one with `pixelSort({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Glitch & signal · tracked as story X6.6 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Passes:** samples the pass input at other positions, so it starts a new merged pass; following pixel effects join that pass. It also renders its own intermediate passes before the merged pass.
- **Masks:** set `effect.mask` to a texture, depth range or selection to limit where it applies; see [masks](/guide/masks).
- **Motion:** Static: nothing animates.
- **Cost:** 454.4 ms added to a 960×540 frame on CI container (SwiftShader software renderer) (2026-10-11). A software renderer: use it to compare effects, not to predict GPU times.
- **Quality tiers:** low: `iterations: 24`, `resolution: 0.25`; medium: `iterations: 40`; high keeps the effect's own values. Set `quality`, or leave it `auto` for an [adaptive composer](/guide/performance).
- **Size:** 7.2 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/pixel-sort`, including the shared effect runtime.

## Credits

Original implementation (MIT). References: Odd–even transposition sort (Habermann, 1972) on the GPU, after Kim Asendorf’s pixel sorting.

## Related

- [Datamosh](./datamosh) — The look of a video with its keyframes removed: motion drags the old picture along in blocks, smearing it into the new one until the next keyframe resets it.
- [Slice shift](./slice-shift) — Cuts the frame into horizontal (or vertical) slices that slide out of line by random amounts, re-cutting a few times a second.
- [JPEG artifacts](./jpeg) — Compresses each frame the way JPEG does (8×8 DCT blocks quantized with the standard tables, color at quarter resolution) and decodes it again, for blocky, ringing, smeared-color artifacts at low quality.
